title: Platform systems & services - how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospective and roadmap (Q4 2025)
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical team wiki for Platform Systems & Services. It aggregates operational how-tos, dashboard and alert guidance, runbooks for common incidents, a short retrospective summary from Q4 2025, and our near-term roadmap. Use this doc as the single source of truth for on-call rotations, ownership boundaries, and the standard operating procedures for platform subsystems (control plane, telemetry, CI/CD, capacity manager).

Owners and contacts

- Platform Systems & Services (eng-platform) - primary owner
- Oncall rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Slack channels: #eng-platform-ops (alerts & triage), #eng-platform-dev (development)
- PagerDuty: Platform Services schedule (see runbook links below)

Summary of scope

This document covers:
- How-tos: onboarding, deploy checklist, run local stack, model serving smoke tests.
- Dashboards & alerts: recommended dashboards, alert thresholds, alert routing policy.
- Runbooks: step-by-step procedures for high-frequency incidents (control plane latency, autoscaler flapping, GPU node OOM).
- Retrospective highlights: Q4 2025 operational learnings and fixes.
- Roadmap: planned improvements and owners through Q2 2026.

How-tos (quick links and procedures)

1) Developer onboarding (new hire checklist)

- Request access: add to GCP project (eng-platform-prod), PagerDuty rotation, and Slack channel.
- Local dev stack: follow the quickstart in docs-site -> eng-platform/quickstarts/local-platform.md.
- Build and run:

  ```bash
  # fetch infra artifacts and start local services
  ./scripts/bootstrap-local.sh --env local --with-telemetry
  make dev-up
  ```

- Smoke tests (post-start):
  1. curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health | jq .status  # expect \"ok\"
  2. ./scripts/run-smoke-test.sh --model small-llm --request-count 10

2) Deploy checklist (control plane / runtime changes)

- Pre-merge: unit tests, integration tests, and perf benchmarks for any runtime-affecting change.
- CI gating: ensure PR has load-test result artifact and a signed performance label.
- Staged rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30 minute hold and SLO checks between steps.

3) Updating dashboards (when adding metrics)

- Add metric to telemetry schema (yaml snippet below).
- Update Grafana dashboard JSON in repo: infra/observability/dashboards/platform-*.json and open PR.
- Notify oncall via PR description and include a one-line summary of expected alert impact.

Telemetry schema example (yaml)

  ```yaml
  - name: control_plane_request_latency_ms
    type: histogram
    buckets: [5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000]
    owner: eng-platform/telemetry
  ```

Dashboards & alerts (current defaults and rationale)

Primary dashboards (Grafana):
- Platform Overview (team-wide): latency p50/p90/p99, request rate, error budget burn, active deployments.
- Control Plane (SRE): API latency histograms, request queue depth, db latency, etc.
- Runtime Health (Serving): GPU utilization, memory pressure, kv-cache hit rates, batch sizes.
- CI/CD Pipeline: average pipeline time, failed builds, tests flake rate.

Alerting policy (high level)

- Severity: Sev1 (PagerDuty) | Sev2 (Slack + email) | Sev3 (email/ephemeral ticket)
- Routing: alerts with impact to <5% error budget and service degradation -> PagerDuty. Non user-facing issues -> Slack/Email.

Key alert thresholds (examples)

| Alert name | Trigger | Initial action | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| ControlPlaneHighP99Latency | p99 API latency > 1200ms for 5m | Escalate to control-plane owner and run latency runbook | eng-platform/control-plane |
| ServingGPUOOM | Any GPU OOM event > 3 nodes within 10m | Scale down affected pool, restart runtime, investigate cause | eng-platform/serving |
| AutoscalerFlapping | 10% scale thrash in 15m window | Pause autoscaler, notify capacity team | eng-platform/capacity |

Note: thresholds above are starting points. Each alert should include runbook link, playbook snippet, and local-execution commands in the alert message.

Runbooks (high frequency incidents)

1) Control plane high latency (runbook)

- Symptoms: external API p99 > 1200ms, queue depth rising, increased 5xx rate.
- Immediate steps (0-5m):
  1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty.
  2. Post incident note to #eng-platform-ops with \"INVESTIGATING: control-plane latency\".
  3. Check control plane pods: kubectl -n controlplane get pods -o wide.
  4. Inspect top traces in Tempo: filter by service=control-plane and latency > 500ms; look for backend DB or rate-limiter spans.

- Mitigation (5-20m):
  1. If DB latency: put read-only fallback for non-critical endpoints (toggle: infra/feature-flags/read-only-fallback).
  2. If CPU saturation on leader: scale replication factor or increase pod cpu request temporarily: kubectl patch deployment control-plane -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"control-plane","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"800m"}}}]}}}}'
  3. If deploy in last 30m: perform immediate rollback to previous revision and monitor.

- Post-incident (RTI): open postmortem if incident > 30m or customer impact > 1% of requests. Link here when created.

2) GPU node OOM (runbook)

- Symptoms: runtime pod restarts with OOMKilled, GPU memory spike.

- Steps:
  1. Identify affected nodes: kubectl get pods -o custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,.status.containerStatuses
  2. Evict non-critical workloads, cordon node: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3. Restart runtime service on node and check driver logs: journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -n 500
  4. If recurrent: open a ticket with infra to run hardware diagnostics and add node to maintenance pool.

Retrospective highlights (Q4 2025)

Top learnings and actions taken:
- Issue: Autoscaler thrash after new batching change caused oscillation in Dedicated pools.
  - Root cause: batching logic reduced request smoothing window; autoscaler reacted to transient drops.
  - Action: added a 3-minute stabilization window to autoscaler and an additional smoothing metric (median batch size). Deployed 2025-11-04.

- Issue: Increased control plane p99 during heavy model onboarding windows.
  - Root cause: synchronous model artifact verification blocking main request path.
  - Action: moved verification to background worker and added artifact prefetch for known publishers (rolled out 2025-12-12).

- Issue: Observability gap for KV cache misses at runtime.
  - Action: added per-model cache miss metric, instrumented sampling traces, created dashboard panels (Runtime -> Cache Efficiency).

Roadmap (next milestones, owners, and success criteria)

Planned items (Q1-Q2 2026):
- Autoscaler v2 (owner: eng-platform/capacity) - implement predictive scaling using request-rate forecasts. Success: reduce scale churn by 40% in 30-day window. Target: 2026-03-31.
- Observability improvements (owner: eng-platform/telemetry) - roll pan-optics dashboard and sampling-based flamegraphs. Success: reduce MTTR for latency incidents by 25%. Target: 2026-04-15.
- Runbook automation (owner: eng-platform/ops-automation) - wire common mitigation steps to runbook actions (Slack buttons to execute safe rollbacks, temporary scale pause). Success: 60% of routine mitigations executed via automated runbook. Target: 2026-05-30.

Roadmap ticket examples and links:
- AUTOSCALER-231 (predictive model) - owner: Priya Nair
- OBS-412 (pan-optics rollout) - owner: Liam Chen
- RUNBOOKS-19 (automation CLI/Slack actions) - owner: Ethan Rodriguez

Operational norms and SLAs (reminder)

- Platform SLOs:
  - Control plane availability: 99.9% monthly
  - Serving runtime p99 latency (normal workload): < 900ms for small models, < 1200ms for medium models
  - Alerting MTTA for Sev1: < 5 minutes

- Change windows: major infra changes scheduled in maintenance windows (Wed 02:00-06:00 UTC). Avoid model-serving runtime changes during top-of-hour traffic spikes (typically 22:00-23:30 PST).

Documentation and where to find things

- Repo locations:
  - infra/observability (dashboards, alert rules)
  - infra/runbooks (markdown runbooks synced to Confluence)
  - infra/manifests (k8s manifests and helm charts)

- Quick links:
  - Platform Overview dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/PLATFORM_OVERVIEW
  - Oncall schedule: https://pagerduty.redwood.example.com/schedules/platform
  - Postmortems index: /confluence/eng-platform/postmortems

Recommended next actions for teams (short list)

1. Ensure all alert runbooks are linked in the alert definitions. (Owner: eng-platform/telemetry)
2. Add sampling traces for any new latency-sensitive endpoints. (Owner: owning service)
3. Review and accept the roadmap tickets in the next planning meeting. (Owner: platform leadership)

Appendix: sample alert rule (Prometheus)

  alert: ControlPlaneHighP99Latency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(control_plane_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 1.2
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
    team: eng-platform
  annotations:
    summary: \"Control plane p99 latency > 1200ms\"
